3: ## Design decisions
4: 
5: - Preserve the supplied public API: `union(intervals: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]`.
6: - Validate every interval before merging; raise `ValueError` when `start > end`.
7: - Sort a new list, then accumulate new tuples in a separate result list so input collections remain unchanged.
8: - Merge when the next start is at most the current end. Closed intervals sharing an endpoint touch; integer neighbors such as `(1, 2)` and `(3, 4)` remain separate.
9: - Extend merged ends with `max` to handle nested intervals. Empty input naturally returns a new empty list.
10: - Sorting takes O(n log n) time; additional space is O(n).

In test_solution.py, tests exercise merging and sorting, empty input, multiple reversed-interval cases, unchanged input after both successful and failing calls, and result-list independence.
